Carlin browse by type volume/amplification compressor browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Carlin Compressor/Fuzz Published on October 21, 2011 Carlin compressor fuzz pedal schematics Information The Carlin Compressor was created in Sweden in 1970 by Nils Olof Carlin as part of the original Carlin Pedals line. It became one of the best known Swedish boutique effects of its era, valued for its ability to combine clean compression with musical overdrive. Unlike conventional compressors that only controlled dynamics, the Carlin design allowed players to blend sustain and distortion in one unit, making it especially appealing to progressive rock guitarists of the time. At the core of the circuit was a JFET used as a voltage controlled resistor, designed to react immediately to note attack while increasing gain as the note decayed. This provided long sustain while maintaining the guitar's natural character. A distinctive feature was the option to introduce harmonic distortion through a second rectifier stage, allowing the sound to move from subtle compression into smooth, singing overdrive without harsh clipping. The result was a versatile effect equally suited to rhythm work, arpeggios, and expressive lead tones. The pedal was housed in a red painted enclosure slightly larger than standard pedals of the day, with three simple controls. It was only battery powered and used a buffered bypass, typical of its time. Carlin Compressors were produced in small numbers and today are considered rare collector's pieces, often remembered for their unique combination of transparency, warmth, and sustain. Controls Sustain : Adjusts the amount of compression and sustain. Dist : Blends in overdrive from clean tones to harmonically rich drive. Volume : Controls overall output level.
